# Code Analysis: `packages/kadi`

Static architecture-health report for the Kadi shared layer. How to read and re-run it:
[../README.md](../README.md). Tool: Archify Code Analysis (pyright-parser 1.1.414 adapter,
`--language py`, locale `en`, update check disabled). First run 2026-11-24 on branch
`wave3/integration`; two fixes followed (ADR-027) and the report was re-run after each.

**Scope.** 48 Python files before the changes, 50 after (test and generated files are excluded by
role: 37 files). Rules that ran: `coupling/import-cycle`, `coupling/cycle`, `coupling/hub`,
`coupling/concentration`, `coupling/internal-leak`, `complexity/function`. Not run: layer
boundaries (none configured) and duplicate detection (needs a separately installed `jscpd`).
275 imports resolved to external packages and are not analysed. The report says nothing about
runtime behaviour.

## Results

| Run | Folder | Findings | Error | Warning | Info |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Baseline (code at git `HEAD` before any change) | `snapshots/2026-11-24-baseline-before-fix/` | 32 | 1 | 9 | 22 |
| 2. After fix 1 (`llm` ↔ root) | `analysis.previous/` | 32 | 1 | 7 | 24 |
| 3. After fix 2 (`kadi` ↔ `ocr`), current | `analysis/` | 32 | 0 | 8 | 24 |

`analysis/` and `analysis.previous/` are rotated by the tool on every run, so they hold the latest
two runs. The baseline is kept separately (the three small JSON files, regenerated by running the
tool on the `HEAD` tree) because rotation would otherwise discard it. Run 1 reported one
`coupling/cycle` error: a 3-module loop, `kadi` → `kadi/llm` → `kadi` (the loop also contained
`kadi/ocr`). Fix 1 left a 2-module `kadi` ↔ `kadi/ocr` error; fix 2 turned that into a warning.

## Fix 1: `kadi.llm` ↔ root cycle (ADR-027)

`kadi/llm/cache.py` imported `kadi.redaction`, a root-level module, while root modules such as
`kadi/extraction.py:17` import `kadi.llm`. `redaction.py` itself imports only `re` and `typing`, so
no *file* looped; the loop was between the `kadi` root group and `kadi/llm`.

- `kadi/redaction.py` moved (`git mv`) to the dependency-free `kadi/privacy/redaction.py`.
- `kadi/redaction.py` stays as a re-export alias, so `from kadi.redaction import redact_pii`
  in `apps/api`, `kadi.clinical_review`, the tests and the docs is unchanged.
- `kadi/llm/cache.py` now imports `kadi.privacy.redaction`.
- Guards: `packages/kadi/tests/test_package_layering.py` and the
  `kadi-llm-and-privacy-below-root` contract in `.importlinter` (6 contracts kept, was 5).

Behaviour is unchanged: the redaction code is byte-identical (a `git mv`).

## Fix 2: `kadi` ↔ `kadi/ocr` cycle, lazy re-export (ADR-027)

`kadi/__init__.py` imported `parse_document` from `kadi/ocr/ocr_parser.py` at the top, and that
module imports the root modules `kadi.line_items` and `kadi.pdf_text_quality`. No file cycle
existed, but `import kadi` pulled in the whole OCR module.

- `parse_document` is now re-exported lazily with a PEP 562 module `__getattr__` (a function-local
  import, plus a `TYPE_CHECKING` import for IDEs). `from kadi import parse_document`,
  `kadi.parse_document`, `dir(kadi)`, `__all__` and `from kadi import *` all behave as before.
- Observable change: `import kadi` no longer loads `kadi.ocr.ocr_parser`, so the OCR module and
  its optional heavy dependencies are loaded on first use. Nothing in the repository imported
  `parse_document` from the package root (all callers import the `kadi.ocr.ocr_parser` submodule).
- **Why the tool still reports it, as a warning:** the lazy import is still an import. The tool
  now classes the loop as "containing deferred, conditional, or type-only edges". It cannot
  happen at import time, because the package root never loads `kadi.ocr`, so the root and the OCR
  module are never initialising each other. The loop would reappear as an error if anyone moved
  that import back to the top of `kadi/__init__.py`.
- Guards: three new tests in `test_package_layering.py` (a fresh interpreter confirms
  `import kadi` does not load `kadi.ocr.ocr_parser`; `parse_document` is the same object by every
  route; unknown attributes still raise `AttributeError`). Reverting to the eager import fails the
  first one. `lint-imports` cannot express "no top-level import of X", so the test is the guard.

`pytest packages/kadi` 678 passed, 6 skipped (672 passed, 6 skipped at baseline; +6 layering

## Still open (not changed)

1. **`kadi/llm/client.py` ↔ `kadi/llm/shadow.py` file cycle (warning).** Real but already
   contained: both sides use function-local imports with comments explaining why
   (`client.py:91`, `shadow.py:117`). It matters only if someone hoists those imports.
2. **Most complex functions (warnings; a maintenance signal, not defects):**
   `assess_text_layer` (`pdf_text_quality.py:211`, cyclomatic 54), `parse_fhir_bundle`
   (`fhir_import.py:119`, 51), `build_case_timeline` (`timeline.py`, 35), `resolve_mention`
   (`resolution/resolver.py`, 30), `calibrate_thresholds` (`resolution/calibration.py`, 26).
   These are tool measurements; the functions were not reviewed here.
3. **Concentration** warnings for `kadi/llm` (3 of 6 other modules depend on it) are a static
   fact about a shared client, not a reason to split it. `kadi/privacy` is the
   most-depended-on module (4 of 6) and, by construction, depends on nothing.
